acceptance_criteria: Design targets exactly one file: src/lua/limiter_wiring_test.zig (test-only change, no production code)
The single immediate assertion at current L600 (`try std.testing.expect(watchdog_state.hasFired());`) is replaced by a bounded retry loop as specified above
Retry mechanism uses either yield-spin with milliTimestamp() deadline, or sleep-based polling with a justified interval -- pick one, do not leave it ambiguous for BACKEND-DEV
Total retry budget is 1000ms, justified as 100x the watchdog's 10ms POLL_INTERVAL_NS and negligible against the test's existing 30s upper bound
Design explicitly confirms the retry loop cannot mask a genuine watchdog failure: the final assertion after the loop still fails the test if hasFired() never becomes true within the budget
Design explicitly confirms no other test (TC-LUA-10-01, TC-LUA-10-02, or the TC-LUA-10-03 mutation check at L603) needs the same fix, with one-line rationale for each

Design artefact is Type E prose (src/design/) or a minimal inline patch description -- classify per templates/lego-catalog.md; given this is a ~6-line test-only change with no new module, a short prose note is sufficient, full Type A-D parameter files are not required

result.summary: Designed test-only fix for GH-600/ISS-0629 (TC-LUA-10-03 flake): replace the single immediate assertion at limiter_wiring_test.zig L600 (try std.testing.expect(watchdog_state.hasFired())) with a bounded yield-spin retry loop (milliTimestamp()-based, 1000ms total budget) that gives the watchdog thread's own 10ms poll cycle a fair window to catch up to an already-expired 1s deadline, without masking a genuine watchdog failure. No production code changes (src/lua/timeout.zig untouched). Confirmed no other test (TC-LUA-10-01, TC-LUA-10-02, TC-LUA-10-03 mutation check) has the same race pattern.
